branches.suitable: Quiet couture portrait or restrained group with garment volume
branches.avoid: Do not default to seated gray-background portrait.
No default blur or obligatory tousled hair.
Do not force rich textile detail into every dark shape.

branches.suitable: User permits experimental loss of descriptive detail
branches.avoid: Not suitable when product detail must remain exact.

relations.rule: Let a restrained bodily action meet a larger garment shape: the difference in scale should be visible, without requiring a theatrical pose.
relations.boundary: Do not copy the flower headpiece, rose shoulder or specific garment; group use is a new extrapolation.

relations.rule: Make the face and the garment separate but connected viewing events; use an edge, hand, collar or bodily turn to connect them, rather than lighting everything equally.
relations.boundary: Quiet does not prescribe a gaze direction, background color or seated posture.

relations.rule: Give skin, near textile and remote edges distinct descriptive strength; retain the chosen viewing anchor without a uniform blur filter.
relations.boundary: Do not infer camera settings; this is not a rule for every work.

relations.rule: Let skin and garment form large interacting light/dark shapes, allowing selective merging with the ground.
relations.boundary: Graphic branch only; not a universal pale-skin or black-garment mandate.

relations.rule: When detail is deliberately reduced, keep a readable organizing shape or color point; make the reduction participate in the subject rather than merely blurring the background.
relations.boundary: Experimental branch; exact source processing remains unknown.

branches.suitable: Fashion scene where a small invented event serves the theme
branches.avoid: One governing event, not a pile of unrelated fantasy props.

branches.suitable: Fashion portrait or pair led by gesture and shape
branches.avoid: No automatic giant object or mandatory saturation.
No forced surreal set when human relations suffice.

relations.rule: Give the garment, ordinary object or room one altered role that the person actually uses; the action must make the scene more than a decorative backdrop.
relations.boundary: Do not reproduce the piano, plane, tea party, mattress tower or saucer; preserve requested person count.

relations.rule: Make contact, support, occlusion and shadows agree with the invented event so it reads as a tangible photographed situation.
relations.boundary: Source production methods are unknown; this is a generative staging decision.

relations.rule: Use framing and bodily directions to turn repeated shapes into a performance; specify color and surface roles only where needed.
relations.boundary: No default hat, red vinyl, primary palette or cropped face.

relations.rule: Let differing head directions, gestures or contact establish the relationship; the people need not share the same gaze or a symmetrical pose.
relations.boundary: Close portrait branch; a single figure can use gesture rather than another person.
